claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a continuous fcc matrix containing dispersed hexagonal C14 Laves-phase precipitates.
Coexistence of the C14 Laves phase with the fcc phase enhances coercivity and suppresses saturation magnetization.
Fe, Co, and Ni moments in the fcc phase couple antiferromagnetically to the Ti-rich C14 phase.
Ti moments align antiparallel to Fe, Co, and Ni moments and thereby reduce the net magnetic moment per atom.
The C14 phase pins magnetic domain walls at fcc/C14 interfaces.
The C14 phase is a high-anisotropy barrier because of its crystal structure and Ti-induced orbital-moment enhancement.
Interfacial strain and electronic hybridization at fcc/C14 boundaries increase the magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant K1.
The increase in interfacial magnetocrystalline anisotropy raises coercivity to approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
The magnetic transitions near 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K arise from decoupling of fcc and C14 sublattices and progressive thermal depinning of domains.
Increasing C14 phase fraction and Ti concentration will increase fcc/C14 interfacial area and strengthen antiferromagnetic coupling.
Crystallographic mismatch and strain at fcc/C14 interfaces create local regions of high magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Domain-wall pinning force scales with fcc/C14 interfacial area and anisotropy contrast.
A dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy will have a saturation magnetization at 400 K that is 15–20% lower than that of single-phase fcc FeCoNiTi.
The transitions at 214 K and 168 K will persist and reflect decoupling of the C14 phase.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNiTi has coercivity capped at approximately 100 Oe because of insufficient orbital moments and a lack of pinning centers.
The proposed mechanism requires a C14 volume fraction above approximately 10 vol% to form a percolating network of pinning sites.
The coercivity enhancement will diminish above the Curie temperature of the C14 phase or if the fcc phase becomes nonmagnetic.
Spin-polarized density-of-states calculations can test whether Ti moments are antiparallel to Fe, Co, and Ni moments in the fcc and C14 phases.

contradictions.description: Rapid quenching is said to produce the dual-phase fcc+C14 initial state, but the proposed comparison also uses rapid quenching to suppress Laves-phase formation and obtain negligible C14 content.

The mechanism attributes enhanced coercivity to fcc/C14 interfaces, so a C14-dominant alloy having lower coercivity than the dual-phase alloy would be compatible with the mechanism rather than falsifying it.
